parts.text: A student investigates an electric circuit to find the resistance of an unknown resistor Z. The student sets up the incomplete circuit shown in Fig. 2.1. There is a gap between the points labelled X and Y. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student: • closes the switch • records the voltmeter reading V 0 • opens the switch. The reading on the voltmeter is shown in Fig. 2.2. Record the voltmeter reading V 0 . Fig. 2.2 V 0 = ...................................................... V [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student: • connects a 10 Ω resistor between points X and Y • closes the switch • records, in Table 2.1, the reading V on the voltmeter • opens the switch • repeats this procedure for resistors of resistances R = 22 Ω, 39 Ω, 47 Ω and 68 Ω. Table 2.1 resistance R / Ω voltmeter reading V / V current I / A 10 1.35 22 2.20 0.10 39 2.85 0.073 47 0.064 68 3.37 0.050

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Use the voltmeter reading in Table 2.1 when the 10 Ω resistor is connected between X and Y to calculate the current I in the circuit. Use the equation: I = V R Record your value of I in Table 2.1 to 2 significant figures. [2]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The voltmeter reading V for the 47 Ω resistor is missing. Calculate V. V = ........................................................... V Add your answer to Table 2.1. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of V / V (y-axis) against I / A (x-axis). Start your axes at the origin (0,0). Draw a best-fit straight line. [4]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
scales labelled with quantity and unit, correct way around
suitable scales (occupying at least ½ the grid)
plots correct to ± ½ small square and precise plots
good best-fit line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Determine the gradient G of your line. Show all working and indicate on the graph the values you use. G = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
indication on the graph as to how gradient found and correct method of calculation of gradient i.e. Δy / Δx
at least ½ the distance between the extreme plotted points used
(ΔI ≥ 0.045)

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) The gradient of your line is numerically equal to the resistance R Z of the unknown resistor Z. Write down the value of the resistance R Z . Record your answer to the nearest ohm. R Z = ..................................................... Ω [1]
